## {background-image="./Images/background-scales_justice_v3.png" .center}

::: {.r-fit-text}
**Section 1: Analyzing International Institutions**
:::

- Week 1: Your Prior Assumptions About International Law

- Week 2: Sources of International Law

- Week 3: Do International Institutions Matter?

- Week 4: Analyzing International Institutions: Legalization

- Week 5: Analyzing International Institutions: Rational Design

::: notes

In the first five weeks of our class I have tried to give you a crash course in analyzing international institutions

<br>

This has meant:

- Unpacking our prior assumptions about international law

- Familiarizing ourselves with how international lawyers and judges define international law

- Examining a VERY old debate in international relations between those who believe international institutions can or cannot have an independent and important effect on global politics

- And then practicing applying two tools that can help us develop empirical tests of the effectiveness of international institutions

<br>

**How are we feeling so far?**

<br>

**SLIDE**: Our plan for next week is to take all your new skills and knowledge and to apply them to an important research question

:::



## Section 2 {background-image="./Images/background-scales_justice_v3.png" .center}

<br>

### How effective have international institutions been in reducing the use of torture by governments around the world?

::: notes

This will not be a toy exercise

- Our aim will be to do this to the best of our abilities

<br>

Over the next six weeks we will:

- Define and measure the outcome of interest: The use of torture by governments

- Unpack the design of the Convention Against Torture (CAT) using the legalization and rational design conjectures

- Analyze the data that connects the CAT to the use of torture by governments

- Unpack the design of the International Criminal Court (ICC) using the legalization and rational design conjectures PLUS adding some insights from principal-agent theory

- And then use case studies of the ICC in action to identify its effect on torture by governments

<br>

**Sound good?**

<br>

Today we wrap up our work with the tools by connecting them to the current world of international problems

- **SLIDE**: We'll use your Canvas submissions as our jumping off point

:::
